theme: Late-October full house: one deep pot of Sunday ragu and a tray of olive-oil autumn vegetables carry the whole kid-friendly week.

components.name: Pork & beef Sunday ragu (sugo)
components.ingredients: 2 lb ground beef (80/20), 1 lb ground pork, 2 onions, 3 carrots, 3 celery ribs, 6 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 cup dry white or red wine, two 28-oz cans whole San Marzano tomatoes, 1 cup whole milk, parmesan rind, bay, olive oil, salt
components.method: Sweat a fine soffritto (onion-carrot-celery) in a generous pour of olive oil over low heat 15-20 min until sweet and silky, add garlic for the last minute. Push aside, brown the pork and beef hard in batches so it really colors, then stir everything together. Add tomato paste and cook it a minute, deglaze with wine and reduce. Add crushed-by-hand tomatoes, milk, parmesan rind and bay; simmer uncovered on the lowest flame 75-90 min, stirring now and then, until glossy and thick. Season. Makes ~2.5 qts; cool and refrigerate, or freeze half.

components.name: Olive-oil roasted autumn vegetables
components.ingredients: 1 large butternut or 2 delicata squash, 1 lb carrots, 2 fennel bulbs, 2 red onions, garlic, rosemary/thyme, lots of olive oil, salt, pepper
components.method: Cut everything into bite-size pieces, keeping the squash a touch larger. Toss generously with olive oil, smashed garlic, herbs and salt across two sheet pans so nothing steams. Roast at 425F for 30-40 min, tossing once, until deeply caramelized at the edges. Cool and store in the fridge; these reheat and recrisp beautifully and become the base for two more dinners.

dinners.name: Rigatoni al ragu
dinners.ingredients: ragu, 1.5 lb rigatoni, parmesan, olive oil, basil or parsley
steps: Boil rigatoni in well-salted water until just shy of al dente; reserve a cup of pasta water.
Warm a big ladle of ragu per person in a wide pan.
Drain pasta, toss into the ragu with a splash of pasta water and a drizzle of olive oil, tossing hard so the sauce clings.
Finish with grated parmesan and torn herbs; serve with more cheese at the table.

dinners.name: Baked polenta with ragu & mozzarella
dinners.ingredients: ragu, 2 cups polenta/cornmeal, parmesan, 1 lb fresh mozzarella, butter
steps: Cook polenta in salted water (and a little milk) until creamy, ~25 min; stir in butter and parmesan.
Spread polenta in a baking dish, spoon over a generous layer of warm ragu.
Tear mozzarella across the top and dust with more parmesan.
Bake at 425F until bubbling and browned, 12-15 min; rest 5 min before scooping.

dinners.name: Roasted-vegetable & white bean minestra
dinners.ingredients: roasted vegetables, two 15-oz cans cannellini, 6 cups broth, parmesan rind, small pasta (ditalini), olive oil, parmesan
steps: Simmer broth with a parmesan rind and one can of beans mashed slightly to thicken.
Add the roasted vegetables and the second can of whole beans; simmer 10 min.
Cook ditalini separately and add to taste, loosening with broth.
Finish each bowl with a hard drizzle of olive oil and grated parmesan; bread on the side for the girls.

dinners.name: Roasted-vegetable frittata
dinners.ingredients: roasted vegetables, 12 eggs, 1/2 cup milk, parmesan or fontina, olive oil, green salad
steps: Beat eggs with milk, cheese, salt and pepper.
Warm olive oil in an oven-safe skillet, spread the roasted vegetables in an even layer and reheat.
Pour in the eggs, cook undisturbed 3-4 min until the edges set.
Finish in a 375F oven 10-12 min until just set; slide out, cut in wedges, serve with a simple olive-oil-dressed salad.

technique.name: Building a proper soffritto
technique.tiedTo: The ragu. The dish lives or dies on the base: dice the onion, carrot and celery finely and evenly, then sweat them low and slow in plenty of olive oil 15-20 minutes until soft, sweet and nearly melting before anything else goes in. No browning, no rushing. Nail it here and the same base lifts the minestra later in the week.

shopping.items: 2 onions, 2 red onions, 1 lb + 3 carrots, 3 celery ribs, 2 fennel bulbs, 1 large butternut or 2 delicata squash, 2 heads garlic, rosemary, thyme, basil or parsley, salad greens
2 lb ground beef (80/20), 1 lb ground pork
1 cup whole milk + extra for polenta, 1 lb fresh mozzarella, parmesan (wedge + a rind), fontina (optional), butter, 1 dozen + eggs

two 28-oz cans whole San Marzano tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato paste, dry white or red wine, two 15-oz cans cannellini, 6 cups broth, 1.5 lb rigatoni, ditalini, 2 cups polenta/cornmeal, olive oil (plenty), bay leaves, salt, pepper

scaleNote: Everything here is already portioned for the full house (2 adults + 4 girls). The ragu batch (~2.5 qts) covers both pasta night and the baked polenta with leftovers, and two sheet pans of vegetables feed the minestra and the frittata. Keep the kids' bowls simple: plain rigatoni with ragu and cheese, polenta scoops, bread alongside the soup. On the lighter two-adult weeks, halve the ragu (1 lb beef / 0.5 lb pork, one can tomatoes), roast a single tray, and push the dinners more adventurous: add chili and pancetta to the ragu, finish the minestra with a poached egg or clams, and swap the frittata for a fennel-and-anchovy version.
